A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TIGER framework and UltraZoom-ST dataset, renamed UZ-ST in v2. All 18 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including supplementary material, are readable. Text extraction and rendered inspection support comparison of equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original Real-CE and UltraZoom-ST experiments, component and training-data ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative restoration results.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds OCR-conditioning ablations, alignment measurements, and multilingual restoration examples.

M1.justification: The two-stage architecture, dual-output text diffusion model, two-phase training, glyph-conditioned image enhancement, and losses in Equations 1–7 remain unchanged. The new ablations test existing components; clarified inference wording and newly disclosed settings do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The synthetic training data, Real-CE, and UltraZoom-ST coverage remain. v2 adds qualitative Japanese and Korean restoration examples in Figure 9, extending language coverage without reporting a corresponding quantitative multilingual benchmark.

E2.justification: The main super-resolution comparator roster is retained. v2 newly evaluates RealSR alignment and single-pass SIFT against its cascade alignment pipeline in Table 8. Table 3 also introduces explicit numerical comparisons against LR inputs through delta OCR-A.

E3.justification: v2 adds null/random OCR-conditioning and empty-mask controls, intermediate OCR-randomness levels, and alignment evaluation on raw 35 mm images using PSNR, MSE, SSIM, NCC, and AKD. Table 3 adds delta OCR-A relative to LR. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, and the OCR-A definition are retained; the revised OCR scores are not accompanied by a stated protocol change.

E4.justification: v1 tests training-data usefulness and three alternative glyph-mask constructions. v2 substantially expands validation with an empty-mask control, null/random OCR tests and a randomness sweep, plus quantitative and visual comparisons of alignment strategies. These additions directly test reliance on semantic conditioning, the contribution of glyph guidance, and the dataset-alignment rationale.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. v2's OCR-randomness percentages describe input perturbations, not uncertainty estimation or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for OCR corruption, empty-mask guidance, alignment, and LR-relative recognition. For example, Table 5 reports 40.4% OCR-A with null text versus 44.6% with predicted text, and Table 6 reports 59.5% with empty masks versus 67.3% for TIGER. Existing OCR values also change: TIGER's 85 mm score falls from 65.8% in v1 Table 6 to 63.2% in v2 Table 11, while its aggregate remains 43.0%. These are revised reported values, not established performance changes from a modified method.

T1.justification: The mathematical method definitions, loss expressions, inference equation, and OCR-A formula remain equivalent. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs. The added empirical metrics and comparisons do not introduce substantive mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies the dataset novelty claim from the first extreme-zoom scene-text dataset to the first Chinese scene-text dataset with extreme zoom. The central claims about text-first two-stage restoration, improved readability and image quality, and state-of-the-art performance remain.

C2.justification: v1 Appendix A.7 explicitly links severe-degradation OCR failures to TIGER failures and states that inference speed is unsuitable for real-time applications. v2 removes that discussion and uses the new OCR ablations to argue limited dependence on recognized text. It retains the narrower efficiency caveat, adds an explanation of cascade alignment's advantages, and extends the applicability discussion to Japanese and Korean.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies a ControlNet conditioning scale of 1.0, elaborates manual filtering or realignment of problematic dataset pairs, and identifies SIFT as the implementation used in the alignment comparison. Existing hardware, losses, learning rates, and epoch budgets remain. The project-page link in v1 Figure 1 disappears, while both versions still promise future code and dataset release.

R1.justification: v2 adds the MTDM paper to the references and related-work discussion, characterizing its text-inpainting approach as limited on complex scripts. The remaining literature coverage and positioning of TIGER relative to general and text-specific super-resolution are largely retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and several explanations are tightened; UltraZoom-ST is generally shortened to UZ-ST; and the duplicated stage name and UltraLens-ST naming error are corrected. Reproducibility and ethics statements move into the reorganized supplement. Most method and comparison prose, and the main section sequence, remain.

P2.justification: The single-column technical report becomes a two-column document with extensively rearranged displays. Tables 2–3 redistribute OCR results and add delta OCR-A, Figure 5 gains an empty-mask column, and new OCR and alignment tables and alignment/multilingual figures appear. v1 Figure 6 is redistributed across v2 Figures 7–8, alongside an additional example.

improvement.justification: The new empty-mask and OCR-corruption controls strengthen validation of the unchanged framework, while the alignment comparison supplies evidence for a dataset-construction rationale that v1 mainly asserted. LR-relative OCR results also clarify the restoration benefit. These gains are partly offset by removing explicit OCR-failure and real-time-deployment limitations, supporting a limited overall improvement.
